Here an ordered symmetric–asymmetric catalytic pair (M sym –M asym , where M is a metal) with subnanometre spacing (~0.5 nm) is reported for urea electrosynthesis, with Cu sym –Zn asym facilitating a yield rate of 233.77 ± 8.89 mmol h −1 g −1 , a Faradaic efficiency of 78.95 ± 4.17%, nitrogen selectivity of >80% and carbon selectivity of >97%. Mechanistic investigations indicate that coordination asymmetry between Cu sym and Zn asym constructs electronically complementary d -orbital configurations that favour the formation of weakly bound *CO on Cu sym , enabling accumulation and migration while suppressing over-hydrogenation. Meanwhile, Zn asym stabilizes *NO, which facilitates coupling with *CO. Subnanometre spacing between metal sites supports stepwise C–N bond formation to urea, and techno-economic analysis indicates the feasibility of low-cost and scalable production. These results verify symmetry-controlled dual-site engineering as a promising strategy for multi-intermediate electrosynthesis.

title: Towards self-driving laboratories in the biopharmaceutical industry
abstract: Self-driving laboratories, which incorporate robotics, advanced sensing, automated feedback control and artificial intelligence, are revolutionizing the conduct of biopharmaceutical research. By coupling high-throughput experimentation with real-time data analytics, these autonomous systems enable rapid exploration of chemical space and adaptive optimization that far outpaces conventional workflows. Here, in collaboration with the Enabling Technologies Consortium, this Perspective highlights the growing importance of self-driving labs for biopharmaceutical discovery and development, drawing on recent industrial applications in solubility screening, solid-form characterization, electrochemical synthesis and lipid nanoparticle formulation. We describe the operational workflow of self-driving laboratories, including key hardware and software components that underpin closed-loop experimentation, and emphasize the critical role of machine learning in guiding experimental design and extracting mechanistic insights from complex data streams. Current barriers, including limited sensor compatibility, data format heterogeneity and the need for integration across diverse instruments, are examined, and strategies for overcoming these barriers are proposed. We envision a future in which continuously learning, data-driven laboratories become foundational infrastructure for accelerating drug development and improving reproducibility across the biopharmaceutical industry.

title: Acid-free activation of acyl hydrazides
abstract: Ferricyanide-mediated activation of peptide acyl hydrazides, at neutral pH, enables their use in ligation chemistry without the need for pH adjustment.

title: Flash Joule heating for rapid MXenes synthesis
abstract: MXenes exhibit interesting structural and physicochemical properties, enabling them to be applied in a wide range of fields, including energy storage and electromagnetic shielding. However, conventional etching synthesis routes, such as hydrofluoric acid etching, Lewis-acid etching and molten-salt etching, are limited by long reaction times, high energy consumption and severe chemical hazards. Here we developed a rapid, scalable and reduced environmental impact approach for MXenes synthesis via sequential flash Joule heating-chlorination and fluorination. By precisely tuning the thermodynamic and kinetic parameters, diverse high-quality layered MXenes with excellent electrochemical performance were synthesized through the selective removal of interstitial atoms from nine different MAX phases, each within 30 s. Computational simulations elucidate the selective-etching mechanism, while high-resolution transmission electron microscopy captures atomic-scale structural evolution from MAX phase to MXene. This universal FJH-ClF strategy reduces energy and reagent usage, establishing a safe, cost-effective and sustainable method for next-generation MXene manufacturing.

title: Orthogonal hydrogenation of alkenes enabled by multifunctional phosphine
abstract: Selective hydrogenation of alkenes is of great importance in organic synthesis, especially for achieving orthogonal selectivity among different alkenes; however, achieving selectivity for poly-substituted sites over less-substituted sites remains an enduring challenge. Given the subtle difference in reactivity and non-preferential coordination characteristics, this selectivity requires both enhancing the system’s catalytic ability and circumventing the susceptible positions. Here we develop a phosphorus-mediated proton transfer strategy that enables completely orthogonal selectivity via the precise differentiation of various alkenes. A multi-role relay of diphenylphosphine plays a crucial role in ensuring this smooth transformation under mild conditions. In addition, a photochemically triggered electron transfer process between alkyl iodides and disubstituted phosphanide ions via charge transfer complexes has also been demonstrated.

title: Asymmetric α-arylation and alkenylation of amines and ethers by a sequential metalation and enantioselective cross-coupling strategy
abstract: Enantioselective C–H metalation coupled with stereospecific cross-coupling is an essential method for forming C( sp 2 )–C( sp 3 ) bonds; however, current protocols typically rely on stoichiometric chiral auxiliaries such as (–)-sparteine, limiting the development of catalyst-controlled strategies. Here we report a sequential C( sp 3 )–H bond metalation/enantioselective C( sp 2 )–C( sp 3 ) cross-coupling strategy that enables Pd-catalysed asymmetric α-arylation and alkenylation of amines and ethers without the need for stoichiometric chiral sources. This approach features readily available reagents and broad substrate compatibility, and delivers both cyclic and acyclic products in high yields and enantioselectivities. Its utility is demonstrated through late-stage functionalization of pharmaceuticals and concise synthesis of chiral ligands and bioactive molecules. Mechanistic studies reveal that the α-arylation of ethers proceeds via dynamic kinetic resolution, whereas that of amines follows a kinetic resolution pathway. Beyond the immediate synthetic utility, we anticipate that this metalation/enantioselective coupling strategy will find application in the functionalization of diverse C–H bonds.

title: Chlorine-mediated electrosynthesis of hydrazine from urea
abstract: Hydrazine is an important chemical widely used in fuels and emerging energy systems, but its industrial synthesis heavily relies on energy-intensive processes involving hazardous oxidants. Here we report a mild and energy-saving electrocatalysis process that enables efficient and selective production of hydrazine from natural urea feedstocks using renewable electricity. This is achieved through a chlorine-mediated urea electrooxidation strategy, where co-adsorbed chlorine and urea can directly couple on the Pt surface to selectively form N -chlorourea. The resulting N -chlorourea subsequently undergoes deprotonation and rearrangement under alkaline conditions, with magnesium hydroxide serving as a catalyst for hydrazine production. In a practical flow electrolyser, this process delivers a hydrazine production of 1.04 mmol cm −2 h −1 and stable operation for 240 h, surpassing previously reported studies. More importantly, the process shows good compatibility with diverse real-world urea-containing waste streams, highlighting its applicability for practical hydrazine production and wastewater valorization.

title: An enthalpy–entropy competition strategy enables moisture-stable and scalable perovskite photovoltaics
abstract: Scalable fabrication of perovskite solar modules is hindered by processing inconsistencies and moisture-induced degradation. Although classic coordination solvents form thermodynamically stable intermediate phases with lead iodide (PbI 2 ) under inert gas atmospheres, they are highly hygroscopic in ambient conditions. Moreover, due to minimal entropy change, this phase is difficult to remove during annealing, leading to micropores and unwanted phases. Here we introduce an enthalpy–entropy competition strategy for scalable, humidity-tolerant perovskite printing, in which dimethyl sulfoxide/ N -methylpyrrolidone is replaced by N -butylpyrrolidone. N -butylpyrrolidone forms strong carbonyl–PbI 2 coordination at ambient temperatures (enthalpy-driven), yet readily dissociates on heating (entropy-driven), facilitating easier formamidinium iodide embedding and intermediate-phase protection. The strategy yields perovskite solar modules with certified power conversion efficiencies of 23.97% in a 100-cm 2 rigid module and 19.71% in a flexible counterpart. Encapsulated devices retain 80% of initial performance after 1,440 hours under the double 85 condition (85 °C, 85% relative humidity), demonstrating outstanding operational durability.

title: Rapid and sustainable MXene synthesis
abstract: MXene synthesis typically takes hours or days. Now, flash Joule heating converts MAX phases into MXenes within tens of seconds through sequential gas-phase chlorination and fluorination. By selectively removing interlayer atoms with reduced acid use, energy input and chemical waste, this approach could offer a fast and sustainable route to diverse MXenes.

title: Traceless sortase ligation for chemical protein synthesis
abstract: Sortase-mediated ligation has emerged as a prominent method for chemical protein synthesis, yet its application is hindered by several inherent constraints, including strict sequence and chirality specificity, reaction reversibility and ligation scars left on the product. Here we report a traceless sortase ligation (TSL) method to overcome these limitations. Our method uniquely features the temporary installation of l -sortase’s natural recognition motifs (LPXTG/GGG) on the reacting partners (one peptide thioester and another N-terminal Cys peptide)—thereby avoiding permanent modifications to the target protein backbone. This approach facilitates efficient intermolecular peptide conjugation via readily available l -sortase, and a subsequent intramolecular native chemical ligation irreversibly traps the ligation intermediate, followed by a quantitative removal of the sortase tags. Consequently, TSL produces homogeneous, ligation-scar-free proteins from a wide range of substrates. The practicality and robustness of TSL were demonstrated by the total synthesis of mirror-image protein CD33-IgC and the semi-synthesis of α-synuclein, showcasing its potential for generating diverse protein targets such as mirror-image proteins and post-translationally modified proteins.

title: Access to all stereoisomers of chiral alcohols with multiple stereocentres enabled by machine learning-empowered protein engineering
abstract: Stereodivergent evolution of a single enzyme into a complete set of stereocomplementary variants capable of accessing all stereoisomers of products bearing three or more newly formed stereocentres remains a major challenge in biosynthesis and protein engineering. Achieving this goal requires precise modification of the enzyme’s active site to impart the subtle differences that govern different stereoselectivities. In addition, screening the vast number of variants in such a complicated evolution task represents another substantial bottleneck. Here we present a stereodivergent evolution of alcohol dehydrogenase from Lactobacillus brevis into a set of stereocomplementary variants that allow access to all eight possible alcohol product isomers bearing multiple stereocentres from the asymmetric reduction of 2,2-disubstituted cyclodiketones. A hybrid rational design–machine learning framework (BioStrucTag) was used, which captures the structural features of the pre-organized catalytic pockets specific for certain chiral products via three-dimensional voxel grid representation of ligand–enzyme complexes. In addition, this framework integrates the enzyme’s sequence features obtained from a transformer-based language model, therefore enabling systematic exploration of sequence space with minimal screening. These variants exhibited outstanding stereoselectivity (up to 99:1 enantiomeric ratio, 99:1 diastereomeric ratio) for most of the tested substrates. Furthermore, crystal structures and molecular dynamics studies revealed the molecular basis of enhanced stereoselectivity switching.

title: Machine learning-empowered enzyme evolution unlocks all stereoisomers of chiral alcohols
abstract: A machine learning-empowered stereodivergent protein engineering platform enables the evolution of a single alcohol dehydrogenase into eight stereocomplementary variants. These variants provide access to all possible alcohol product stereoisomers bearing multiple stereocentres in the asymmetric reduction of 2,2-disubstituted cyclodiketones.

title: A fast and energy-efficient catalytic pathway for stainless steel synthesis
abstract: Hydrogen-assisted reduction facilitates an enhanced reaction rate between nickel and iron oxides, enabling the direct production of Fe–Ni master alloys.

title: Accelerating synthesis at scale requires a coordinated ecosystem
abstract: The pace of materials discovery is increasingly determined by how quickly candidate materials can be made, characterized, and validated at scales relevant to real applications. Sustaining progress will require not only technical advances but also a coordinated ecosystem of standards, shared data, and translational infrastructure across sectors.

title: Conductive three-dimensional molecular-cluster networks via rare-earth-directed assembly
abstract: Molecular-based crystalline conductors provide well-defined structural platforms for probing how molecular arrangements govern electronic properties, yet conventional zero-dimensional cluster materials generally exhibit low conductivity owing to the difficulty of establishing efficient conductive networks within isolated systems. Here we show that electron-rich dimeric molecular conductors are constructed by introducing the quasi-aromatic metal-cluster building blocks {Mo IV 3 -py 3 } (where py represents pyridine) as stereogenic units and encapsulating rare-earth ions. This design enables the formation of d – π ··· π – d conjugated conductive pathways between isolated clusters. Among the systems studied, hexagonal phases incorporating Sm and Eu exhibit the shortest π ··· π distance (3.66 Å) and the highest in-plane conductivity (approximately 3 × 10 − 5 S m − 1 ), over 10 5 × higher than conventional polyoxometalates. Rare-earth incorporation promotes the formation of a semiconducting hexagonal phase and a metallic-like tetragonal phase, while also enabling the modulation of anisotropic charge transport in single crystals. This work not only extends the application of rare-earth elements beyond their conventional roles in magnetism, luminescence and catalysis but also provides a rational design strategy for the tailored construction of cluster-based crystalline materials with targeted electronic properties.

title: Nanoconfined electrocatalytic CO2 reduction
Combining CO2 and bicycloalkanes for polyester production
Designing heterogeneous electrocatalytic sites using reticular chemistry
abstract: Catalytic activation of small molecules offers opportunities for sustainable energy conversion and storage, addressing the demand for carbon-neutral energy sources. This need has prompted the development of advanced heterogeneous electrocatalytic systems that are capable of efficiently driving these molecular transformations. Consequently, substantial progress has been made in explaining the structural and functional characteristics of catalytically active sites and their influence on electrochemical performance. However, the molecular-level understanding and manipulation of the immediate microenvironment surrounding heterogeneous catalytic centres, and its role in governing electrocatalysis, remain limited. To address this knowledge gap this Review discusses recent developments, showing how reticular chemistry can regulate the proximal chemical environment of active sites, thereby influencing electrocatalytic activity and selectivity. Moreover, as the field progresses towards more complex multi-electron and proton-coupled reactions, emerging challenges and reticular chemistry-based approaches for overcoming them are outlined.

title: Author Correction: Accelerating synthesis at scale requires a coordinated ecosystem
Modular assembly of bioisosteric bridged aza-frameworks via ring strain release
abstract: Recent advancements in synthetic chemistry have sparked substantial interest in bridged compounds, particularly azabicyclo[ x .1.1]alkanes (ABCAs), which have emerged as critical structural motifs in medicinal chemistry. These compounds are highly valued for their unique geometric constraints, enhanced target selectivity and favourable pharmacokinetic profiles. However, despite their importance, the construction of diverse ABCA motifs remains challenging, because existing methodologies are often limited to specific ring systems and substituents. Here we present a modular synthetic strategy for the construction of ABCA motifs. The key to this approach lies in the successful synthesis of a series of highly strained azatricycloalkanes, such as 1-azatricyclo[4.1.0.0 2,7 ]heptane. By leveraging stereocontrolled transformations of the strained C–N bonds within these azatricycloalkanes, we have synthesized a wide range of ABCA derivatives with high structural diversity. This methodology has been utilized in the development of orexin receptor antagonists and bioisosteres, showcasing its potential to advance drug discovery for therapeutic applications.

title: Author Correction: Gram-per-litre-scale production of lutein by engineered Corynebacterium
A coumarin-linked conjugated covalent organic framework for enhanced photocatalytic hydrogen evolution
abstract: Photocatalytic water splitting holds promise for addressing the global energy challenge, although the solar-to-hydrogen efficiency remains limited by rapid electron–hole recombination. Here we report on the design and one-pot synthesis of a conjugated covalent organic framework (COF) photocatalyst featuring coumarin linkages created by the polycondensation of phenylacetonitriles with o-hydroxybenzaldehydes. The coumarin linkage largely enhances the planarity and conjugation of the COF backbone compared with their imine- and vinyl-linked counterparts, thereby decreasing radiative recombination upon light irradiation. The coumarin-linked COF achieves an apparent quantum yield of 37.95% at 405 nm and a photocatalytic hydrogen production rate of 531.2 mmol g −1 h −1 under 440-nm excitation, rivalling state-of-the art organic photocatalysts. Transient absorption spectroscopy reveals that the coumarin linkage extends the lifetime of long-lived charge-separated states by approximately 1,000-fold to 1,080 ps, compared with 1.07 ps for the imine-linked COF. These long-lived charges rapidly transfer to the cocatalyst within 407 ps, driving hydrogen production. These findings highlight the critical role of linkage chemistry in determining the photocatalytic performance of conjugated COFs.

title: Meet the editors
abstract: The six editors of Nature Synthesis outline their key topics of interest within the scope of the journal.

title: Strain-release strategy for access to diverse azabicyclic bioisosteres
abstract: Azabicyclo[x.1.1]alkanes (ABCAs) are useful motifs in medicinal chemistry but difficult to construct. Now, a strain-release strategy that uses strained azatricycloalkanes enables the modular, stereocontrolled synthesis of diverse ABCA bioisosteres. This approach is validated by the synthesis of orexin receptor antagonists and constrained azetidine analogues.

title: Enantioselective synthesis of chiral 2-azaspiro[3.3]heptanes and their application as piperidine bioisosteres
abstract: With the increasing emphasis on ‘escape from flatland’ in medicinal chemistry, contemporary efforts are increasingly directed towards three-dimensionally shaped, F sp 3 -rich frameworks over aromatic systems to enhance drug-like properties and expand patentable chemical space. Despite growing interest in piperidine bioisosteres, catalytic approaches to these scaffolds remain comparatively underdeveloped and catalytic methods for their asymmetric synthesis are even rarer. 2-Azaspiro[3.3]heptane has emerged as a promising F sp 3 -rich piperidine bioisostere with an enhanced three-dimensional shape. However, no catalytic methods for the asymmetric synthesis of 2-azaspiro[3.3]heptanes have been reported so far. Here we report the asymmetric synthesis of 2-azaspiro[3.3]heptanes from commercially available substrates, using an enantioselective reductive amination process enabled by chiral phosphoric acid catalysis. A series of enantioenriched 2-azaspiro[3.3]heptanes were obtained in high yields and with excellent enantioselectivities. Computational calculations elucidated possible reaction pathways and the origins of enantioselectivity. Onward synthetic transformations can form valuable chiral building blocks for concise syntheses of pharmaceuticals and an IRE1α inhibitor bioisostere exhibiting enhanced inhibitory activities and improved absorption and metabolism properties.

title: Rethinking selectivity in alkene hydrogenation
abstract: Although catalyst development has transformed alkene hydrogenation into a reliable synthetic tool, controlling regioselectivity between closely related alkenes continues to challenge even the most sophisticated catalytic systems. Now, a multifunctional phosphorus-mediated proton relay directs priority towards more substituted alkenes, delivering divergent products under exceptionally mild conditions

title: Chemoselective Ni-catalysed directed C(sp2)–H alkylation at low temperature using alkyl sulfonylhydrazides
abstract: Here we report a method for facile C–H alkylation of a range of (hetero)arenes under Ni-catalysis. This reaction takes place at 50 °C, is scalable, tolerates heterocyclic substrates and can be applied to both primary and complex secondary alkyl donors. Success hinges on the use of sulfonylhydrazide-based alkyl donors that mildly generate alkyl radicals, thereby obviating the need for alkyl-halide precursors that require harsher conditions to activate. The demonstrated substrate scope is broad (>70 examples), and the reaction is also applied to natural product synthesis. Mechanistic studies (both computational and experimental) suggest that an asynchronous, amine-assisted C–H activation pathway is operative.

title: Through-space conductive pathways for polyoxometalate electronics
abstract: Three-dimensional through-space charge-transport pathways are constructed through an assembly of quasi-aromatic clusters, transforming insulating polyoxometalates into intrinsic molecular conductors.

title: Enantio- and diastereoselective synthesis of multi-helical nanographenes
abstract: Nanographenes, composed of two-dimensionally fused planar polycyclic aromatics, are promising candidates for organic optoelectronic applications due to their high chemical and thermal stability and efficient charge transport. However, their high planarity often leads to aggregation and poor solubility. Introducing helicene units at the nanographene periphery is an effective strategy to enhance solubility and impart chiroptical functionality. Here we report the enantio- and diastereoselective synthesis of hexabenzocoronene-based helical nanographenes bearing up to eight uniformly aligned helicene units via enantioselective [2+2+2] cycloaddition followed by a diastereoselective Scholl reaction. Systematic variation of aryl substituents within this synthetic platform affords a family of multi-helical nanographenes with tunable photophysical and chiroptical properties. A helical nine-armchair graphene nanoribbon bearing six peripheral helicene units is also accessible, exhibiting near-infrared emission with high fluorescence quantum yield and a distinct chiroptical response. Together, these results demonstrate a versatile platform for constructing complex chiral nanographenes with precise helicity control.

title: Crystallization control for narrow-linewidth perovskite LEDs
abstract: A carefully selected underlayer coupled with a simple film-processing technique is shown to create a controlled crystallization environment that enables ultranarrow-linewidth emission in green and blue perovskite LEDs.

title: Electroreductive oxime carboxylation with CO2 produces arylglycines
abstract: A two-step electrosynthetic pathway for arylglycine production from aldehydes, nitrite and carbon dioxide (CO2) has been developed. The method avoids using traditional approaches involving cyanides, harsh conditions or specialized biocatalytic approaches.

title: Electrosynthesis of arylglycines from carbon dioxide, nitrite and aldehydes
abstract: Arylglycines, such as phenylglycine, are an important class of high-value unnatural amino acids that play essential roles in medicinal chemistry. Yet, their traditional synthesis relies on highly toxic reagents, harsh reaction conditions, or delicate biological or enzymatic routes. Here we develop a reductive carboxylation reaction for converting oximes and CO 2 into amino acids via Lewis acid-assisted electrocatalysis, which enables a two-step electrosynthesis route producing arylglycines from low-cost feedstocks including CO 2 , nitrite and aromatic aldehydes. In the process, nitrite is electrochemically reduced to hydroxylamine, which condenses with the aldehyde to form an oxime. The oxime subsequently undergoes electroreductive carboxylation to generate the arylglycine product. Using benzaldehyde as a model aldehyde substrate, phenylglycine is synthesized with an overall Faradaic efficiency of 81% and with 84% conversion. Oxime carboxylation proceeds via an imine intermediate, where metal ion coordination is crucial for reactant activation, intermediate stabilization and product separation. Mechanistic analysis identifies the rate-determining step as the first electron transfer that leads to N–O bond cleavage under Lewis acid activation. This electrosynthetic system shows a broad substrate scope that can lead to a diverse range of heteroaromatic glycines.

title: Sustainable pyrrole synthesis
Hierarchically porous metal–organic frameworks with red topology for hydrogen and methane storage
abstract: The construction of highly porous metal–organic frameworks with complex topologies requires precise matching between linker conformation and node connectivity. Here we report the reticular design and synthesis of CU-6-M (M = Fe or Cr), assembled from conformationally adaptive diphenylethynyl linkers and six-connected trinuclear oxo-centred clusters. The ability of the linker to adopt multiple out-of-plane conformations satisfies the geometric requirements of a red topology, resulting in a highly interconnected hierarchical pore architecture. CU-6-Fe and CU-6-Cr exhibit an interconnected hierarchical pore system with Brunauer–Emmett–Teller surface areas up to 7,145 m 2 g −1 . This architecture enables total H 2 uptakes of up to 17.5 wt% and 45.4 g l −1 at 100 bar and 77 K. Under temperature–pressure swing conditions, CU-6-Fe and CU-6-Cr deliver up to 16.9 wt% and 44.1 g l −1 and also show record gravimetric CH 4 storage at ambient temperature. These results establish linker flexibility as a key design parameter for the realization of complex, highly porous topologies for high-capacity storage of clean-energy fuel gases.

title: Author Correction: Chemical reactivity from the perspective of enthalpic coupling
Geometric frustration in morphologically chiral nanoribbons of layered perovskites
abstract: Twisting and chiral growth are unusual in crystals and rarely observed in layered materials. Here we show that layered achiral metal-halide perovskites spontaneously form twisted and helical ribbons. Microscopy, diffraction and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that hydrogen-bonded organic networks within the lattice generate mismatched strains, causing ribbons to bend and twist when the strain is released, similar to the chiral opening of seed pods. This mismatch, known as geometric frustration, originates from crystal symmetry and can be tuned through molecular doping. Controlling growth kinetics twists nearly all ribbons towards one direction, giving bulk samples chiroptical activity. Statistical and mechanical analyses show that ribbon shape is governed by intrinsic elastic strain and geometric constraints; modulating them enables a continuous transition from twisted to helical ribbons. Our results show how molecular-scale interactions can generate macroscopic chiral shapes, providing a route to control chiral morphologies in layered two-dimensional materials.

title: Accelerated polymer design outpaces resistance
Programming membranes with ice
abstract: Ice-mediated interfacial growth enables the synthesis of programmable microcapsules with tunable membrane properties for biocatalysis.

title: Descriptor-informed multi-component doping enables high-performance Co-free Ni-rich cathodes
abstract: Co-free Ni-rich layered oxide cathodes hold great promise for cost-effective, high-energy lithium-ion batteries, but their practical application remains limited by sluggish Li + kinetics and rapid capacity fading. Although doping has been widely used to mitigate these issues, conventional trial-and-error dopant selection remains inefficient for guiding rational materials development. Here we move beyond empirical dopant screening by developing a descriptor-informed multi-component dopant selection strategy based on dopant charge density and metal–oxygen bond strength. Low-charge-density dopants reduce electrostatic barriers to Li + migration, while high-bond-energy dopants reinforce the oxygen sublattice and stabilize the metal–oxygen framework. This doping strategy simultaneously accelerates Li + kinetics, suppresses cycling-induced phase transitions and mitigates chemomechanical fatigue, thereby delivering exceptional electrochemical performance in Co-free Ni-rich cathodes. The enhanced apparent Li + transport and structural stability enable an ultrahigh-rate capability of 130.9 mAh g −1 at 25 C and at 25 °C, excellent cycling retention of 82.4% after 350 cycles at 10 C and robust low-temperature operation delivering 112.2 mAh g −1 at 1 C under −20 °C. These findings, transitioning the design principle from empirical or trial-based selection to a targeted selection regime, present a promising route for developing high-performance cathode materials for lithium-ion batteries.

title: Propionic acid synthesis via room-temperature coupling of ethane and CO
abstract: Directly converting light alkanes into higher-value oxygenates under mild conditions remains challenging due to the inert nature of C–H bonds and competing pathways that lower selectivity. Here we report an ethane–CO coupling strategy over a Cu catalyst in dilute acid and in the presence of molecular oxygen, enabling the selective synthesis of propionic acid at room temperature. CO acts both as a coupling partner that intercepts C–H activation intermediates and as a selectivity-modulating agent. Adsorbed oxygen species on oxidized Cu facilitate ethane activation, while Cu + released from the surface oxide into the acidic solution facilitates the formation of CO-derived species that are engaged in C–C bond formation. Propionic acid formation rates up to 120 μmol \({\rm{g}}_{\rm{Cu}}^{-1}\;{\rm{h}}^{-1}\) are achieved with a selectivity of 50%. At lower propionic acid production rates, an optimal selectivity of 83% is reached. This work establishes CO-mediated alkane carbonylation under mild conditions as an effective synthetic strategy for the production of organic acids.

title: Ice-mediated interfacial membrane synthesis of cargo-independent microcapsules
abstract: Membrane-defined compartmentalization enables selective transport and protects biomacromolecules in living systems, yet synthetic microcapsules remain difficult to fabricate because existing methods are often harsh, multistep or cargo-specific. Here we report an ice-mediated interfacial reaction platform that programmes membrane growth on ice-sphere templates to generate closed microcapsules with cargo-independent encapsulation. During ice recrystallization, monomers preloaded within the ice matrix are enriched into the quasi-liquid layer, where they undergo confined interfacial amidation with a complementary organic-phase monomer to form a conformal polyamide membrane. Melting the ice releases intact microcapsules with encapsulated cargo retained. The resulting microcapsules exhibit tunable membrane thicknesses (7–260 nm) and diameters (30–500 μm), and function as confined microreactors for multienzyme redox cascades, achieving up to an 80-fold enhancement in visible-light-driven CO 2 -to-methanol conversion. This strategy provides a mild and potentially scalable route to programmable semipermeable microcompartments.

title: Photoelectrochemical C(sp3)–C(sp3) cross-coupling using native functional groups
abstract: Radical–radical cross-coupling provides an attractive strategy for constructing C( sp 3 )–C( sp 3 ) bonds directly from simple feedstocks. However, the diffusion-controlled nature of radical recombination and the sensitivity of transition-metal catalysis to the reaction redox environment have limited the generality of such transformations across diverse substrate classes. Here we report a photoelectrochemical method for selective C( sp 3 )–C( sp 3 ) cross-coupling using native functional groups. By decoupling alkyl radical generation from catalytic redox maintenance, this strategy integrates photoinduced ligand-to-metal charge transfer for mild radical formation with electrochemical regulation of the catalytic redox balance. In combination with Fe–Ni dual catalysis, the system enables diverse double decarboxylative, dehydroxymethylative and deformylative cross-couplings directly from carboxylic acids, alcohols and aldehydes without pre-activation, accommodating primary, secondary and sterically hindered tertiary carbon centres. Mechanistic studies indicate that a sacrificial alkyl bromide prevents over-reduction of nickel, sustaining a Ni(II)/Ni(III) catalytic cycle that mediates selective radical cross-coupling via S H 2 radical sorting.

title: Publisher Correction: Electrosynthesis of arylglycines from carbon dioxide, nitrite and aldehydes
Modular synthesis of 3,3-diaryloxetanes
abstract: Oxetanes are strained four-membered oxygen heterocycles that are valuable motifs for modulating lipophilicity, metabolic stability and three-dimensional structure of pharmaceuticals. Diaryloxetanes with 3,3-substitution are recognized as bioisosteres of diaryl ketones that preserve key electronic features while exhibiting distinct reactivity. However, synthesis of this motif largely relies on Lewis acid-promoted Friedel–Crafts reactions, which are restricted to electron-rich arenes and often suffer from low functional-group tolerance and competing side reactions. Here we report a method for the synthesis of 3,3-substituted diaryloxetanes from readily available 3-oxetanone through a cross-coupling reaction with tetrafluoropyridone as leaving group. The difunctionalization through subsequent addition of two aryl groups, one from an aryl halide, the other from an arylboronic ester, provides access to a variety of benzophenone bioisosteres. The nickel-catalysed cross-coupling at a fully substituted carbon centre is enabled through oxetanyl C–O bond oxidative addition and establishes programmable entry to 3,3-diaryloxetane bioisosteres that are synthetically challenging to access via traditional polar bond disconnection strategies. Mechanistic studies support a Ni(0)-mediated oxidative addition of the oxetanyl tetrafluoropyridine ester.

title: The road to self-driving laboratories in industry
abstract: In this issue, we focus on the development of self-driving laboratories for the autonomous synthesis of molecules and materials, with a particular focus on industrial considerations and applications.

title: Scrambling-free synthesis of heteroleptic silylium ions by halide abstraction from halosilanes
abstract: Heteroleptic silylium ions with different substituents at the silicon atom are generally not accessible using established tools for producing such reactive intermediates because substituent exchange reactions occur in acidic media, leading to homoleptic silylium ions with three identical alkyl and aryl substituents, respectively. Here we report a broadly applicable route to heteroleptic silylium ions using halosilanes as silylium ion precursors, which are less prone to that scrambling process. While this deceptively simple method has failed so far owing to the lack of a suitable halide-abstracting agent, superhalophilic halogen-substituted silylium ions enable smooth halide abstraction from a diverse set of halosilanes at ambient temperature without substituent redistribution. Accordingly, this approach provides access to essentially any heteroleptic acyclic as well as cyclic silylium-ion motif from common halosilanes, including trialkyl-, dialkyl(aryl)-, alkyldiaryl- and triaryl-substituted congeners. Computational calculations reveal the mechanism of heteroleptic silylium-ion formation and the origin of the suppressed substituent-scrambling process.

title: One-step skeletal editing of oxetanes to thietanes using thiourea
abstract: Heteroatoms fundamentally shape the physicochemical and biological properties of bioactive molecules. However, accessing heteroatom-edited analogues typically requires laborious de novo synthesis, thereby constraining rapid exploration of therapeutic opportunities. Here we report a one-step skeletal editing strategy that directly converts readily available oxetanes into thietanes using thiourea. This transformation enables direct atom swapping in a single operation, exhibiting broad substrate scope and functional group tolerance, and compatibility with structurally complex, drug-like molecules, thereby facilitating exploration of thietane chemical space. Combined experimental and computational studies support a cascade pathway involving oxetane activation, regioselective ring opening, rearrangement and intramolecular cyclization, providing mechanistic insight into this O-to-S skeletal editing process.

title: Photocatalytic tetrapeptides for enantioselective visible light-induced transformations
abstract: Research on enantioselective photocatalysis has so far been focused on molecular photocatalysts or large yet easily adaptable photoenzymes. However, both catalysis classes display deficiencies either due to their limited adaptability or their high molecular weight. Here we show that small peptides can bridge the gap between the currently used photocatalysts by combining structural flexibility and low molecular weight. We constructed a small peptide that displays a pyroglutamic acid at its N terminus for substrate recognition. At the C terminus, a thioxanthone-based amino acid was installed to harvest photons and to act catalytically by energy transfer. Two amino acids were sufficient to link the two components, resulting in a photocatalytically active tetrapeptide that was used both for photochemical deracemization and enantioselective [2 + 2] photocycloaddition reactions. Our results demonstrate that small peptides with a molecular weight below 750 Da can act as efficient molecular catalysts for enantioselective photochemical transformations.

title: A general synthesis of tryptophan-crosslinked macrocyclic peptides enabled by a dual-functional directing group
abstract: Tryptophan-crosslinked macrocyclic peptides have recently emerged as an exciting class of natural products with intricate structures and therapeutic properties. Although their biosynthesis and biological functions have been explored, simple and broadly applicable chemical methods for their total synthesis are not available. Here we describe a general approach for the synthesis of these rigid and complex peptides using rhodium-catalysed intramolecular transannular macrocyclization. The success and broad applicability of the approach rely on a mechanistically guided design and detailed computational analyses of the catalytic cycle, which arrived at a dual-function nucleophilic pyridyl directing group that enabled ortho -metalation and nucleophilic carbon–nitrogen bond formation in complex molecular settings. This directing group can be easily installed using cross-coupling chemistry, carried over peptide coupling sequences and removed after formation of the desired macrocycle. We demonstrate the utility of this method by synthesizing, among others, the pharmacophores of micitide 982 and the potent antibiotic tryglysin.

title: Synthesis of chiral allylic amines through regio- and enantioselective homologation of enamines using Ni catalysis
abstract: Enantioenriched aliphatic allylic amines are ubiquitous substructures in natural products and bioactive molecules and serve as useful chiral building blocks for the synthesis of value-added targets owing to the orthogonal reactivity of multiple reactive sites. Therefore, catalytic methods for the synthesis of aliphatic allylic amines from readily available starting materials are highly desirable. Here we report the development of a method for the regio- and enantioselective homologation of enamines, enabled by Ni-catalysed cross-coupling of enamines with alkynes, providing access to enantioenriched allylic amines. The reaction features enantioselective C( sp 2 )–C( sp 3 ) cross-coupling to form enantioenriched allylic amines with chemo-, regio- and enantioselectivity control. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the reaction is enabled by a selective hydrometallation of electron-rich alkenes over more electrophilic linear alkynes. Notably, the process provides a convenient synthetic route to a wide range of bioactive molecules and key intermediates, highlighting the utility of the process.

title: Enantioselective synthesis of π-extended carbo[17]helicene via sequence-controlled quadruple [2+2+2] cycloadditions
abstract: The enantioselective synthesis of giant chiral nanocarbons composed solely of carbon and hydrogen remains a central synthetic challenge. Increasing molecular strain, steric congestion and loss of cyclization sequence control have prevented access to enantioenriched long π -extended carbohelicenes. Here we report the enantioselective synthesis of a π -extended carbo[17]helicene enabled by a programmed precursor for quadruple [2+2+2] cycloadditions followed by oxidative annulations. The sterically differentiated dodecayne incorporates two inner triyne units forming less congested [5]helicenes and two outer triyne units forming sterically demanding [6]helicenes. These triyne units are separated by a triphenylene backbone that modulates steric demand and enforces sequence from the molecular centre. This sequence-controlled annulation suppresses dead-end pathways and enables stepwise assembly of the helicene framework with high enantioselectivity. The resulting carbohelicene exhibits circularly polarized luminescence with g lum values of up to 0.043. This study highlights steric differentiation and cyclization programming as useful design strategies for the enantioselective synthesis of large helical nanocarbons.

title: Atomically ordered dual atomic pairs in CuAuZn2 intermetallics for efficient urea electrosynthesis
abstract: Electrochemical C–N coupling from CO 2 and NO 3 − offers a sustainable route to produce urea, but kinetic mismatches between carbon and nitrogen intermediates limit selectivity and production rates. Here we report the synthesis of atomically ordered copper–gold–zinc (CuAuZn 2 ) intermetallic catalysts with high densities of Cu–Zn and Au–Zn dual atomic pairs (DAPs). The Cu–Zn sites facilitate nitrate reduction to *NH 2 , while the neighbouring Au–Zn sites enhance CO 2 reduction to *COOH and subsequent urea formation. The atomically ordered CuAuZn 2 electrode achieves 85.5% ± 1.6% Faradaic efficiency and 50.1% ± 1.5% energy efficiency for CO 2 and NO 3 − co-reduction at 0 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode. Under membrane electrode assembly conditions, it operates for 1,000 h at 100 mA cm −2 with a urea yield rate of ~8.3 mg h −1 cm −2 . The ordered DAPs can be extended to other C–N coupling reactions and offer sustainable electrosynthesis routes towards high-value amides. This work highlights the development of atomically ordered DAPs for C–N bond formation and suggests a design principle for multi‑intermediate catalysis towards sustainable chemical production.

title: Mechanoradical-chain C(sp3)–C(sp2) coupling with unactivated arenes
abstract: Solvent-free mechanochemistry enables reactivity and selectivity, which are difficult to achieve in solution, particularly for poorly soluble polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. Here we describe a mechanochemical radical-chain C( sp 3 )–C( sp 2 ) coupling between benzyl halides and unactivated arenes that proceeds with high regioselectivity across a broad range of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and enables direct post-functionalization of poly( N ‑vinylcarbazole). Spin-trapping and radical-clock experiments support the in situ generation of benzyl radicals during milling and a radical-chain propagation manifold. To provide a qualitative physical picture for force-assisted C–I homolysis, we introduce an atom-probe computational model in which controlled compressive distortion increases the diradical character and destabilizes benzyl iodides, consistent with mechanoradical formation under milling. A coupling product further serves as a precursor for on-surface synthesis, and an unexpected nanographene isomer was found, highlighting the synergy between mechanochemistry and atomically precise nanocarbon synthesis. Collectively, this work provides a prime example that mechanoradicals, often considered detrimental in material design, can be harnessed for constructive and highly selective C–C bond coupling in the solid state.

title: Hydrogel-confined environment for aqueous-compatible perovskite crystallization
abstract: Halide perovskite synthesis generally uses toxic, high-boiling-point and strongly coordinating organic solvents, hindering scalable processing and crystallographic control in thick-film applications. Water is ideal as a solvent but incompatible with perovskite synthesis due to precursor insolubility and rapid hydrolysis in water. Here we introduce a hydrogel-confined reaction environment that overcomes this incompatibility by decoupling precursor solvation from lattice formation. Within a polymer–water network, PbI 2 and organic iodides are dispersed in a stabilized ionic state that suppresses aggregation and kinetically inhibits water-induced decomposition. Concurrently, this network anchors emerging nuclei and imposes spatial confinement, directing crystal growth into dense thick films. Spectroscopic and computational analysis reveals facet-specific coordination between polymer and perovskite, suppressing surface defect formation and preserving efficient charge transport despite the presence of the polymer matrix. The resultant thick hydrogel-grown films (180 µm) exhibit charge carrier mobilities of ∼10 cm 2 V −1 s −1 . When directly integrated into pixelated X-ray imaging sensors, the device achieves a high sensitivity-to-noise ratio of \(25,000\,\upmu {\text{C}}\,{{\text{Gy}}}_{{\text{air}}}^{-1}\,{{\text{cm}}}^{-2}\,{{\text{pA}}}^{-1}\) , with an ultralow detection limit of 19.8 nGy air s −1 , enabling high-fidelity imaging with negligible signal crosstalk.

title: Synthesis of covalent organic frameworks through hydrogen-bonding catalysis
abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are a class of crystalline, porous networks constructed by polymerization of organic building blocks. However, most COF syntheses developed so far rely on acid- or base-catalysed reactions that are sensitive to monomer structure, require extensive condition screening, proceed under harsh conditions over several days and often yield low-quality products. Here we report a general hydrogen-bonding catalysis strategy enabled by benzimidazole and its derivatives, acting as both hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors, to produce high-quality COFs. Distinct from conventional catalysis, these catalysts interact with monomers, intermediates and transition states, thereby reducing energy barriers at each step and promoting reversibility. This approach enables control through catalyst-to-monomer ratios and allows the rapid synthesis, within hours, of imide-, imine-, hydrazone- and sp 2 -carbon-linked COFs with high crystallinity and porosity. The method further supports catalyst reuse and 1,000-fold scale-up, producing COFs with benchmark proton conductivity, establishing hydrogen-bonding catalysis as a versatile route for scalable COF synthesis and applications.

title: Reversible zinc oxidation as a route to on-demand hydrogen delivery
abstract: The transition to green hydrogen is limited by the absence of efficient synthetic pathways for on-demand, high-purity hydrogen at decentralized locations. Most solar and wind resources are located far from demand centres, and the infrastructure costs of hydrogen pipelines make them economically unfeasible for widespread deployment. Here we report a reversible energy vector-mediated synthetic pathway that uses metallic zinc for hydrogen distribution. Machine learning-guided screening identified lactate as a ligand that outcompetes hydroxide for Zn(II) coordination in alkaline media, doubling the soluble Zn(II) concentration to 1.12 M and enabling self-sustained, circuit-free hydrogen production. The system operates between 0 and 80 °C with approximately 99% Faradaic efficiency and achieves a volumetric hydrogen capacity of 137.9 to 218.4 kg H 2 m −3 , exceeding, to the best of our knowledge, many established and state-of-the-art carriers. This approach offers improved safety and practical deployment compared with existing carriers, providing on-demand green hydrogen for remote communities, mobile platforms and off-grid industrial sites.

title: Topotactic synthesis of gradient-encoded covalent organic framework membranes
abstract: Embedding continuous chemical gradients into single-phase crystalline reticular membranes remains synthetically challenging, because the reversible chemistry required to establish long-range order generally drives the system towards spatial uniformity. Here we report a topotactic gradient-programming strategy that decouples lattice formation from subsequent chemical diversification. A reversibly assembled, vertically aligned precursor membrane is subjected to diffusion-limited solid-state linkage conversion, which progressively reprogrammes pore-wall chemistry across the membrane thickness while preserving the parent topology, membrane continuity and crystalline alignment. By kinetically trapping intermediate conversion states, this process writes through-thickness chemical gradients into aligned nanochannels. The strategy is shown across compatible reticular chemistries, enabling gradient-encoded β-ketoenamine-, imide-, enaminone- and olefin-linked frameworks. Using imine-to-β-ketoenamine conversion as a model, the resulting axial chemical asymmetry creates a spatially varying ion–wall interaction landscape that enables direction-dependent ion transport, near-unity cation selectivity even under a 1,000-fold concentration gradient, a 12-fold enhancement in osmotic energy-conversion efficiency relative to compositionally uniform analogues and retained structural integrity after exposure to 12 M HCl. This study establishes diffusion-limited topotactic conversion as a platform for programming continuous chemical gradients in crystalline reticular membranes.

title: The synthetic evolution of porous liquids
abstract: Porosity has long been considered a property exclusive to solids, yet a new class of materials now combines permanent, well defined pores with the ability to flow. Realizing the full promise of these materials as ‘supersolvents’ will require a deeper understanding of the liquid–pore interface and continued exploration of understudied designs, alongside their translation into separation, catalysis, sensing and therapeutic applications.

title: Introducing chemical gradients into crystalline porous membranes
abstract: Diffusion-limited conversion of pre-formed covalent organic framework membranes creates a continuous chemical gradient across their thickness, with linkage conversion increasing from one face to the other while preserving aligned crystalline nanochannels. This asymmetry directs selective ion transport and increases salinity-gradient energy conversion, while the formation of robust linkages improves acid stability.

title: Straightforward on-demand synthesis of heteroleptic silanes
abstract: The stepwise installation of carbon substituents at silicon starting from tetrachlorosilane or tetraalkoxysilanes is burdened by chemoselectivity issues, typically affording product mixtures. Now, monoselective bromination of multihydrosilanes followed by nucleophilic displacement opens the door to the programmable and reliable synthesis of functionalized silicon building blocks.

title: Stepwise and chemoselective installation of carbon substituents at silicon atoms via monobromination of hydrosilanes
abstract: Although organosilicon compounds containing different carbon substituents are ubiquitous in synthetic chemistry, their preparation is challenging. Laboratory synthesis commonly relies on the sequential substitution of tetrachlorosilane or tetraalkoxysilanes, producing complex mixtures that require demanding purification. This arises from limited control over nucleophilic substitution in functionalized silanes containing three or four (identical) leaving groups. Here we introduce an experimentally straightforward and reliable procedure for the preparation of both hetero- and homoleptic silanes using an overlooked monobromination of primary and secondary hydrosilanes. An equimolar amount of elemental bromine converts a Si–H bond into an Si–Br bond without ‘overbromination’. This step also shows exceptional functional-group tolerance to existing substituents at the silicon atom. Unsaturated moieties as well as heteroatom and heteroaryl groups are compatible. When performed in an iterative fashion, multihydrosilanes can be selectively converted into secondary, tertiary and quaternary silanes with two, three or four different carbon substituents in high yields. These functionalized silicon building blocks are relevant to synthetic chemistry as well as applied chemistry materials.

title: A solution for metal–organic cages
Manipulating dissolved gases with porous liquids
abstract: By creating permanent cavities of well-defined size and shape within a fluid, porous liquids bring the precise control over gases afforded by microporous solids to the realm of liquids. Here, we reflect on how the porous liquid concept, beyond simply imparting fluidity to a porous solid, provides a promising platform for overcoming long-standing challenges with manipulating dissolved gases.

title: Durable, highly loaded atomically dispersed catalysts via a reticular coordination strategy
abstract: Developing catalysts that can support high metal loadings (>10 wt%) that are resistant to sintering under harsh reaction conditions remains a fundamental challenge. Here we present a reticular coordination strategy to maximize precious metal utilization where Pt atoms are anchored onto Ce-oxo clusters within metal–organic frameworks and then converted into Pt RC /CeO x (where RC denotes reticular coordination) by calcination, yielding catalysts with high atomic dispersion (14.9 wt%). Upon high-temperature (>300 °C) treatment under H 2 , the isolated Pt species do not undergo uncontrolled sintering; instead, their migration is suppressed after limited restructuring into flat, strongly confined ultrasmall clusters. Using the treated material (0.15 mg Pt cm ‒2 ) in proton exchange membrane water electrolysers results in a degradation rate of 25 μV h ‒1 , which outperforms 40 wt% Pt/C (106 μV h ‒1 at 0.40 mg Pt cm ‒2 ) and retains its structural integrity after 500 h at 1 A cm ‒2 .

title: A Fischer-type uranium carbyne
Thianthrenium ylides for safe carbene transfer
Understanding porous liquids
abstract: Becky Greenaway, Associate Professor (Reader) and Royal Society University Research Fellow at Imperial College London, talks to Nature Synthesis about developing automated high-throughput experimentation to design porous liquids as well as persistent challenges in the field.

title: The physical chemistry behind porous liquids
abstract: Margarida Costa Gomes, CNRS Research Professor at École Normale Supérieure de Lyon, talks to Nature Synthesis about understanding the molecular behaviour of porous liquids and the challenges of translating that understanding into functional materials.

title: A seed-confined strategy to alloy immiscible systems for methanol oxidation
abstract: The design of high-performance alloy catalysts is constrained by thermodynamic immiscibility among constituent elements (for example, W–Bi). High-entropy designs can overcome immiscibility by incorporating multiple elements, but active sites are often diluted and structure–property relationships are obscured. Here we report a compositionally minimalist seed-confined alloying strategy that uses a single thermodynamically selected seed, rather than multiple additional alloying elements, together with pathway-controlled alloy formation. Pt was selected as a representative seed because favourable Pt–W and Pt–Bi interactions improve ternary alloying accessibility while providing active sites for methanol oxidation; pre-anchoring creates dispersed incorporation centres, promotes multi-element association and suppresses competing phases. The resulting WBi–Pt@B/C catalyst comprises dispersed, robust nanoparticles with a diameter of ~3.6 nm and delivers a mass activity of 13.41 A per mg Pt in methanol oxidation, retaining 94.1% of its activity after 5,000 cycles. This strategy provides a practical route to the construction of compositionally simple nanoscale alloy catalysts with chemically complementary functions.

title: Bridging molecular and enzymatic photocatalysis
abstract: Asymmetric photocatalysis generally relies either on compact molecular catalysts or much larger photoenzymes. Now, a photocatalytic tetrapeptide, combining a substrate-binding site and a visible light-absorbing photosensitizer within a modular scaffold, enables highly enantioselective photochemical transformations.

title: Combining anionic and neutral ligands for kinetic stereocontrol in nickel catalysis
abstract: Precise stereochemical control of substituted cyclohexanes is pivotal in drug discovery, where distinct stereoisomers dictate divergent biological activities. While methods to access thermodynamically favoured cyclohexanes are well established, stereoselective synthesis of their disfavoured counterparts remains underdeveloped. Here we present a dual-ligand nickel-catalysed platform that enables three-component 1,1-arylfunctionalization of substituted methylenecyclohexanes with high kinetic stereocontrol. The cooperative interplay between an anionic and a neutral ligand is crucial for dictating stereochemical outcomes. This strategy exhibits broad substrate scope, accommodating aryl and alkenyl bromides as well as N -sulfenyl- N -alkyl sulfonamide ([N–S]) reagents to form thermodynamically disfavoured 1,2- cis , 1,3- trans and 1,4- cis isomers with high efficiency and selectivity. Experimental and computational studies reveal that the thermodynamically disfavoured cyclohexanes are formed preferentially, underscoring the critical role of the external ligand in controlling stereoselectivity during the Ni–H migratory insertion step. The practicality of this approach is further demonstrated through the rapid and concise synthesis of biologically relevant molecules.

title: Catalyst regeneration enables durable electrochemical ammonia cracking for H2 production
abstract: Ammonia (NH 3 ) represents a promising hydrogen (H 2 ) carrier because it is easily stored and transported. Subsequent electrochemical NH 3 cracking offers a sustainable route for downstream decentralized H 2 production, but its activity and durability are limited by oxidation and nitrogen poisoning of platinum-based catalysts during anodic NH 3 oxidation. Here we show that platinum nanoparticles supported on nitrogen-doped carbon containing atomically dispersed iron sites (Pt/Fe-NC) resist both deactivation pathways and achieve an NH 3 oxidation mass activity of 733 A g Pt −1 . Electron transfer from the support suppresses platinum oxidation and accelerates the rate-determining dehydrogenation step. More importantly, the Fe-NC substrate promotes a water-assisted in situ regeneration pathway that enables the hydrogenation of poisonous *N into reactive NH-containing intermediates for dimerization. Combined with pulsed electrolysis, intermittent acid washing and NH 3 replenishment, this catalyst sustains H 2 production for over 2,000 h at 10 mA cm −2 and 500 h at 1.5 A cm −2 .

title: AI-guided discovery of self-assembled monolayers combining synthetic accessibility and interfacial stability for perovskite solar cells
abstract: Navigating the vast chemical space to discover self-assembled monolayers that combine synthesizability, interfacial compatibility and long-term device stability remains a large challenge in perovskite photovoltaics. Here we present an artificial intelligence-guided design framework for self-assembled monolayers that integrates graph neural network-based retrosynthetic predictions with high-throughput screening based on density functional theory and expert chemical knowledge. Over 90,000 structures from 308 fragments were narrowed down to 300 candidates, ranked using a composite score of eight descriptors extending beyond intrinsic electronic properties to include synthesizability, hole reorganization energy λ h and structural features (heteroatom content and aromaticity). The top candidate, AI-1, is readily synthesizable and incorporates favourable heteroatom functionalities. AI-1 achieves optimal energetic alignment and forms robust S–Pb coordination bonds at the buried interface, effectively suppressing non-radiative recombination and enhancing interfacial stability. Devices incorporating AI-1 achieved a power-conversion efficiency of 27.2% and retained >95% of their initial efficiency after 2,000 h of maximum-power-point tracking at 65 °C. Mechanistic studies show that the multifunctional methylthio side chain is vital, as it reinforces the interfacial bonding and balances passivation with chemical robustness. These findings demonstrate that artificial intelligence-guided design can systematically deliver self-assembled monolayers uniting high efficiency with long-term operational stability, and they provide general principles for interface engineering.

title: Magnetic-field annealing of compositionally complex alloys
Electrifying hydroformylation
Design principles for porous liquid synthesis
abstract: Porous liquids represent a distinct class of porous materials in which permanent porosity is realized in fluid states, extending synthetic control beyond the traditional constraints of crystalline or crosslinked frameworks. Here we establish a synthesis-focused approach that unifies the chemical principles governing porous liquid formation. Their development hinges on retaining accessible voids while preventing pore occlusion and phase separation. We survey advances across four archetypes of porous liquid, including discrete porous molecules, solutions of rigid porous scaffolds, dispersions of porous solids and molten porous networks. These systems can be understood through two principles: exclusion of the surrounding liquid from intrinsic cavities, and stabilization of porous hosts within a fluid phase. Strategies such as corona–canopy engineering, electrostatic complexation, supramolecular assembly and colloidal stabilization address porosity–fluidity trade-offs and enable multiscale porosity and adaptive chemistry in porous liquids, whereas emerging high-throughput computational approaches are beginning to accelerate their discovery.

title: Liquid-phase growth of dense ceramic films
abstract: Ceramics are a class of materials that serve as a cornerstone for frontier technologies, such as electronics, solid-state batteries and materials for the aerospace industry. However, ceramics suffer from severe elemental volatilization and degradation during high-temperature sintering. Liquid-phase densification is a promising strategy to address these challenges, but the approach has remained unrealized. Here we report on a mild liquid-phase growth method used to prepare fully dense, compositionally uniform, proton-conducting ceramic films (melting point exceeding 2,700 °C) in a molten-salt system without external pressure. The liquid-phase growth mechanism was revealed by real-time monitoring as a sequence of melting, dissolution and reaction, nucleation and growth stages. Further fuel-cell testing validated the gas-tightness and favourable electrochemical functionality of the liquid-phase-grown electrolyte. This strategy decouples film densification from high-temperature solid-state sintering and provides a pathway towards on-demand ceramic synthesis.

title: Enhanced neutral seawater photoelectrolysis by fast hydrogen pumping at subnanometre triple interfaces
abstract: Hydrogen production from neutral water is promising for directly using abundant seawater, yet remains challenging because of sluggish reaction kinetics induced by limited hydrogen supply and transfer to active sites. Here we design a catalyst system consisting of atomically dispersed Cr(OH) x clusters on Pt-decorated GaN nanowires for photoelectrochemical splitting of neutral seawater. The triple-interface architecture (Cr(OH) x –Pt//Cr(OH) x –GaN//Pt–GaN) couples water activation, hydrogen transfer and Pt–H formation across adjacent interfaces, enabling a fast hydrogen pumping process. Through this process, the challenges associated with hydrogen supply and transfer are addressed, surpassing the kinetically limited hydrogen utilization on the conventional single-interface systems. A photocurrent density of around 100 mA cm⁻ 2 and more than 50 h of operational stability are achieved under neutral saline conditions with concentrated sunlight at 0 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode. In a hydrazine-assisted seawater photoelectrolyser, the photocathode enables a bias-free photocurrent density of ~70 mA cm −2 . This work establishes multi-interface hydrogen management as a promising strategy towards practical hydrogen production.

title: Expanding atropisomerism to C–P bonds
Synthesis of atomically thin amorphous materials
abstract: Atomically thin amorphous materials (ATAMs) combine atomic-scale thickness with the absence of long-range in-plane periodicity, encompassing layered two-dimensional amorphous materials and non-layered atomically thin amorphous films. These materials lack in-plane translational and orientational order yet retain distinct short- and medium-range atomic order within their film-like configurations. The scalable synthesis of ATAMs is essential for advancing both fundamental understanding and technological deployment, bridging the gap from the laboratory to the factory. Here we discuss ATAM synthesis from a mechanism-guided perspective, including thermodynamic suppression, kinetic freezing, template induction and defect- or ion-driven amorphization. We then establish links between local disorder descriptors with functional properties, compare controllable and scalable production strategies and examine outstanding challenges related to stability, standardized performance metrics and wafer-scale integration. Finally, we outline artificial-intelligence-assisted closed-loop strategies for application-targeted scalable synthesis and wafer-scale manufacturing. By integrating mechanistic insights with scalable fabrication principles, here we aim to provide a roadmap for the synthesis and deployment of emerging ATAMs and to offer a forward-looking perspective for accelerating progress in this rapidly evolving field.

title: Deaminative nucleophilic substitution of alkyl amines
abstract: Nucleophilic substitution is one of the most fundamental and widely used strategies for alkyl functionalization. For more than a century, such transformations have relied predominantly on alcohols and alkyl halides as the primary alkylating synthons. Here we report a nucleophilic substitution strategy that uses the unique reactivity of N -alkyl nitroamines, enabling alkyl amines to serve as a latent and readily available class of direct alkylation reagents. Through a systematic investigation of N -alkyl nitroamine reactivity, we have developed a polarity-driven platform for direct deaminative functionalization, enabling broad nucleophilic substitution of alkyl amines to efficiently construct alkyl C−halogen, C−C, C−N, C−O and C−S bonds. The method accommodates primary, secondary and tertiary alkyl amines as well as benzylic amines. This strategy overcomes the intrinsic limitations of aliphatic diazonium chemistry and substantially expands the scope of nucleophilic substitution reactions hitherto inaccessible by conventional approaches.
